newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut Yankee plant's fate seen decided early Nov.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut Yankee plant's fate seen decided early Nov.

text.p: Owners of the Connecticut Yankee nuclear power plant will likely decide on whether to mothball the generating facility in early November, said the operator Connecticut Yankee Atomic Power Co.
"It's safe to say the next couple of weeks," replied plant spokesman Anthony Nericcio when asked about a time for the announcement of Connecticut Yankee's fate.
"The owners want to get on with this thing," he said.
The plant's owner on Oct 9 recommended mothballing the 582 megawatt generating station in Haddam Neck, Conn., after an economic analysis showed it has become too costly to run.

"It is in the ratepayers' interest to shut the unit," said Nericcio, referring to the conclusion of the analysis, and added there are cheap energy sources that could replace the output if Connecticut Yankee were permanently shut.
Meanwhile, the plant's owners continued to evaluate data from the analysis before making a decision, he added.
Connecticut Yankee was shut July 22 amid safety concerns raised following a Nuclear Regulatory Commission inspection of the facility.
Connecticut Yankee is owned by eight New England utilities, with Northeast Utilities the main shareholder with a 49 percent stake.

Other owners include New England Power Co at 15 percent, United Illuminating Co (9.5 percent), Boston Edison Co (9.5), Central Maine Power Co (6.0), Montaup Electric Co (4.5), Cambridge Electric Light Co (4.5), and Central Vermont Public Service Corp (2.0).
Cambridge Electric Light is a subsidiary of Commonwealth Energy System, and Montaup Electric a divison of Eastern Utiliities Associates.
